objective_for_doctor: A 109-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lightheadedness/near-fainting, feeling nauseous or do you feel like vomiting, and diarrhea or an increase in stool frequency.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having lightheadedness like I might faint, and I feel nauseous—like I could vomit. I also have diarrhea with more frequent stools, and I got a pink itchy rash with swelling on my skin, including around my mouth and on my arms and neck.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the symptoms start (hour/day), and have you had any new food, medicines (especially antibiotics/NSAIDs), or insect/seasonal exposures in the past 1–2 days?  
Doctor: Also, does the rash itch like hives and do you have any trouble breathing, wheezing, or lip/tongue swelling beyond the skin swelling?

It started about 1 day ago. In the 1–2 days before this, I ate dark-fleshed fish or Swiss cheese. The rash is very itchy—like hives—and it’s pink with swelling (about a 4/10). I don’t have trouble breathing or wheezing, and I don’t have lip or tongue swelling beyond what’s on my skin.

Doctor: Given the timing (1 day after possible food trigger), itchy hive-like rash with swelling, plus nausea/near-fainting and diarrhea, do you feel your heart racing or have you had low blood pressure symptoms (dizziness when standing)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vitals_Orthostatics_and_O2Sat, REQUEST TEST: CBC_CMP, REQUEST TEST: Serum_tryptase (if available within 4–6 hours of onset).
Yes, I feel dizzy/lightheaded when I stand, like my blood pressure might be low. I’m not sure about my heart racing—I haven’t really checked my pulse.

Doctor: Thanks—do you currently have any fever, severe abdominal pain, or black/bloody stools, and have you taken any new medications today (including aspirin/ibuprofen) since the symptoms began?  
Doctor: I’m going to treat this as likely anaphylaxis with GI involvement—can you tell me if you have ever had a similar reaction before, and do you have access to an epinephrine auto-injector or have you taken any antihistamines already?

I don’t have a fever, and I don’t have severe belly pain. I haven’t noticed black or bloody stools. I didn’t take any new medicines today, and I don’t have an epinephrine auto-injector. I haven’t taken antihistamines yet. I don’t think I’ve had anything like this before.

Doctor: Based on your symptoms (hive-like itchy rash with swelling, GI symptoms, and lightheadedness on standing after a possible food trigger) this is most consistent with **anaphylaxis**—do you have a thermometer and can I ask your current pulse/blood pressure if you can check, and are you able to sit up safely right now?  
Doctor: **REQUEST TEST: Blood_glucose** (before treatment) and **REQUEST TEST: ECG** (to check heart rhythm/ischemia as part of near-fainting).  
Doctor: While we check, I’m preparing to treat immediately—have you received any medications yet today, and can you tell me if you can take an injection (no severe bleeding disorder), so I can proceed with **IM epinephrine** promptly.

I don’t have a thermometer with me right now. I haven’t checked my pulse or blood pressure yet. I can sit up safely right now.  

I haven’t received any medications yet today, and I can take an injection if needed.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your rapid-onset hives with swelling plus nausea/diarrhea and near-fainting with standing after a likely food trigger, this is high-risk for anaphylaxis, so I’m going to treat now; I’ll give **IM epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mg** (adult dose) and then observe closely.  
Doctor: Can you confirm: are you feeling worse or improving right now, and do you have any worsening throat tightness/hoarseness, shortness of breath, or cough?
I think I’m still about the same or a little worse—my dizziness is still there. I don’t have throat tightness, hoarseness, shortness of breath, or cough.

Doctor: Since you’re still worsening and you have hives with swelling plus near-fainting after a likely food trigger, this remains **high-risk anaphylaxis** even without breathing symptoms—are you able to receive IM epinephrine now (and repeat if symptoms persist), and do you have any history of heart disease or are you on beta-blockers?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Repeat_Vitals_in_5min_after_epinephrine, REQUEST TEST: Repeat_Pulse_Oximetry.
Yes, I can receive the injection now. I don’t have a history of heart disease that I know of, and I’m not on beta-blockers.

Doctor: I’m giving **IM epinephrine now** for high-risk anaphylaxis—then we’ll recheck your vitals/oxygen shortly; after that I’ll also give antihistamine (and consider steroids) while we monitor.  
Doctor: Do you have someone with you who can call emergency services/transport you to the ER now, and can you confirm you can safely lie down with legs raised if you feel faint?
I’m here with someone who can call for transport to the ER. If I feel faint, I can lie down and raise my legs.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as ongoing high-risk anaphylaxis—please lie down with legs elevated, and we’ll give epinephrine and then supportive meds while your companion calls emergency services/transport to the ER now.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Anaphylaxis (food-triggered) with GI involvement and urticaria/angioedema causing near-syncope (hypotension/vasovagal concern).
